edges.description: Failure of calcium binding is proposed to compromise CL-K1 during biosynthesis and prevent secretion. Cellular quality-control recognition and degradation are plausible intermediates that were not directly demonstrated.

Calcium normally stabilizes ligand-binding loops in the carbohydrate-recognition domain. The tested variants lose calcium binding and carbohydrate recognition; loop destabilization links these molecular effects.

CL-K1 depletion disrupts neural crest distribution in zebrafish, and recombinant protein attracts neural crest cells in explants. The responding receptors and intervening signaling steps are unresolved.

Collectin-11 loss impairs osteoclast differentiation in experimental cells, with species- and complement-background-dependent effect sizes. Recombinant CL-11 partially rescues differentiation; the intervening signaling steps and their relevance to skeletal disease in 3MC patients remain incompletely established.

Reduced CL-L1 availability is proposed to disrupt craniofacial cell guidance. CL-L1 attracts HeLa cells and is expressed in developing palatal tissue, but a CL-L1-specific neural crest receptor or signaling route was not established.

Reduced CL-L1 chemoattraction provides a candidate explanation for the developmental phenotype of the Cys270Serfs*33 patient. Transfer from the HeLa assay to neural crest migration remains inferential.

masp1 knockdown alters neural crest migration in zebrafish, supporting a role for this locus in guidance. The developmental substrate of MASP-3 and the contribution of the other isoforms remain unresolved.

edges.description: Colec11/C3 and Colec11/Cfb bone-marrow cultures show marked impairment of osteoclast differentiation and partial rescue with recombinant CL-11. The living double-knockout animals provide an associated bone-maintenance phenotype, rather than proof that the measured osteoclast defect causes their bone loss.
edges.limitations: Additional complement-gene deletion is not the usual human 3MC genotype. Only overtly affected double knockouts underwent CT or histology; phenotype incidence may therefore underestimate subclinical lesions. Detailed lesions were concentrated in vertebrae, with no detected skull-calvarial abnormality or significant femur-length difference. Colec11/C3 embryos lacked overt morphological abnormalities by E18.5. Results do not establish a cause of human developmental synostoses or craniofacial malformations. The reported ex-vivo differentiation/rescue experiments specifically tested Colec11/C3 and Colec11/Cfb, not all three double-knockout genotypes.

nodes.description: Experimental loss of collectin-11 impairs osteoclast differentiation in mouse bone-marrow cultures and engineered healthy-donor human iPSC-derived cells. The effect is modest after isolated mouse Colec11 deletion and pronounced in Colec11/C3 or Colec11/Cfb double-knockout cultures; isolated human COLEC11 deletion already has a marked effect. Recombinant CL-11 partially rescues differentiation, and complement-convertase inhibition impairs differentiation in human cells. These results identify a candidate mechanism relevant to 3MC, without establishing osteoclast dysfunction as the cause of skeletal malformations in affected patients.
